doc.title: Mose Allison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: The service station jukebox and the country blues
summary: Allison heard Tampa Red, Memphis Minnie and Big Bill on the jukebox while working at the store.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: I’m referring to some interviews here... I understand that people would socialize and come together at both the service station and the general store. I think you said that the service station had a jukebox?
Something incomprehensible to northerners. Can you talk about that?
Yeah. Well, that’s where I heard the country blues, and early. I used to go there when
I was working at the general store, and I used to go over and listen to the jukebox. It had a lot of blues players...
I think in one interview you mentioned Tampa Red.
Now, could you identify them at that time for who they were? Were you listening on that level, or was it...
I didn’t know anybody... I didn’t know about them.
Mose left Tippo... You were very young when you really moved out, once you went to college. Right?
And you went to the Army before that.
